title: Relative Verdier biduality on dualizable objects for an invertible relative dualizing complex
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $k$ a field of positive prime characteristic different from $\ell$, and $a:X\to S$ a morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. In the actual condensed bounded constructible categories of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], with internal Hom of [def-sfb-dc-tensor-hom-adjunction] and exceptional inverse image of [sk-def-sfb-dc-upper-shriek], put $W=Ra^!\mathbf{1}_S$. Suppose that $W$ has a two-sided tensor inverse and that $K$ is dualizable. Then the specified map $K\to\operatorname{RHom}(\operatorname{RHom}(K,W),W)$, the transpose of braided evaluation, is an isomorphism. This is conditional and does not claim that $W$ is dualizing for every base or that every bounded constructible object is dualizable.

source.place: Proof, double application of the invertible twist comparison and coefficient biduality; categorical implementation in WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Closed/InvertibleDualizing.lean, isIso_toIhomIhom_of_isDualizable

proof.text: Apply the existing categorical theorem CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.isIso_toIhomIhom_of_isDualizable with T=W, gamma=Iso.refl W, the given invertibility of W and dualizability of K. Its proof identifies the double dual relative to W with coefficient biduality by tensoring the coefficient dual with W and using its inverse. The theorem has no geometric premise and applies to the actual condensed category, without identifying it with the etale coefficient categories.

The two named morphisms are definitionally equal: verdierBiduality unfolds to Verdier.bidualityMap W K, and both it and MonoidalClosed.toIhomIhom W K are curry of the braiding followed by the internal-Hom evaluation. Thus exact the categorical theorem closes the stated IsIso goal. No use is made of the disputed unrestricted isIso_verdierBiduality.
